semantic_checks: The functions are actual complex-valued functions of a real variable, real analytic on the full open interval (-r,r), with r>0 explicit.
The given identity is f(t)+|t| times g(t)=0 on that interval. It does not separately assume either coefficient vanishes.

Positive and negative open subintervals give local vanishing of the real-analytic functions f+t g and f-t g, respectively. The pinned analytic uniqueness theorem on the connected interval extends both identities to the whole interval.

Their difference gives t g(t)=0 on a positive neighborhood. Since t is nonzero there, g vanishes on that neighborhood; analytic uniqueness extends its vanishing through t=0 and throughout (-r,r). The plus identity then gives f=0.
Both sides of zero are actually used. Neither a one-sided analytic assumption nor division by t at zero is hidden in the proof.
